PY.behavior: Console script dispatches Click index; folder defaults to dot and is expanded/resolved; analysis precedes opening storage.
Directory validation needs no Git; root gitignore enables nested Git rules, atlasignore always applies; fallback exclusions and root containment filter discovery.
Filename language detection excludes C/C++; supported files are sorted and read as raw bytes.
Sequential parsing hashes original bytes, replacement-decodes UTF-8, extracts structure/imports/calls; dedicated-adapter syntax diagnostics differ from fatal parser exceptions.
Callable metrics run after parsing and before relationship resolution.
Resolution handles imports, inheritance, calls with deduplicated external unresolved/ambiguous targets, not runtime execution proof.
A validated in-memory schema-v2 artifact contains hierarchy/relationships, views, diagnostics, counts and repository metadata; asdict passes it to storage.
Canonical local location reuses a registration; URL locations are skipped and new folder-derived names receive collision suffixes.
SQLite path is configurable; foreign keys, busy timeout and explicit transactions are configured; schema migration is separate, not implicit on service opening.
Saving upserts graph metadata/revision and replaces normalized graph rows rather than storing the full artifact blob or appending history.
New registration and graph are atomic; replacement exceptions roll back; analysis failure cannot overwrite an existing graph.
After commit stdout is repositoryId/schemaVersion/stats only; selected exception classes become Click errors, not all exceptions.

TS.behavior: Root manifest dispatches Bun/TypeScript indexing and import; Python/legacy guidance is not a subprocess in that runtime chain.
Browser form posts name/location, invalidates repositories on success and displays mutation errors.
POST rejects malformed JSON; registration trims/limits fields, uses UUID/time and returns 201 or duplicate-name 409 with case-insensitive uniqueness.
Registration stores metadata only; location is reference-only, no clone/index/import automatically; list joins import timestamps.
Terminal import reads supplied JSON locally and calls the service directly; usage/file/parse/service errors print and set exit code 1.
Schema-v2 artifact validation checks nodes/hierarchy/references/edges/cycles without rebuilding or discarding original metadata.
Import validates before a transaction, resolves exact ID before case-insensitive name, and upserts one artifact/timestamp; failures preserve the prior graph.
Bun SQLite/Drizzle stores complete JSON by repository FK, uses configurable/cwd-relative database, WAL/FKs/migrations; importer and server must target the same DB.
Architecture GET requires ID (400), unknown registration is 404, unimported is null, otherwise stored artifact; unexpected errors are generic 500.
Explorer hides tests, projects direct relationships for the current scope rather than precomputed views, and lazy-loads the React Flow canvas.
Graph route separately renders loading/error/null/data and keys the explorer by repository ID/import time; retained data can coexist with a refetch error.
Graph query is keyed by ID with retry false; manual refresh refetches graph and repositories; terminal import has no browser push invalidation/polling in this code.

EX.behavior: Create event reloads player, validates weekly_orders through Player changeset, flashes invalid input; UI window gating is not enforced by handler and positivity is absent.
Factory skips order creation; weekly update/session/window closure occurs separately after successful submission, and weekly-update failure does not undo committed orders.
Create transaction locks board players in ID order, chooses retailer-to-wholesaler-to-factory supplier, creates PENDING PLAYER_ORDER and RECEIVING/SENDING joins; errors abort.
Creation publishes association order_created notifications only after transaction success, not inside its writes.
Deliver event delegates assigned player ID; transaction casts/locks order, authorizes SENDING caller, requires PENDING/exact participant shape, sorted player locks, same board and sufficient stock.
Delivery debits sender, credits receiver and last_order for user orders, marks DELIVERED; CPU has no receiver.
Delivery writes roll back on transaction errors; postcommit players/order notifications are outside rollback protection; old Boards.deliver_order is not the routed path.
Connected LiveViews subscribe to global order/player/scheduled topics; player updates are filtered by assigned player ID.
order_created adds only matching SENDING orders, not RECEIVING joins.
order_updated replaces only already-listed IDs; histories deduplicate, sort ID descending, cap each at ten; initial session loading reconstructs both.
30-second jobs broadcast commands consumed by connected views; CPU creates sender-only order/demand transaction without cpu-flag gating; factory produces stock, not automatic delivery.
live_session_updated notifications reload session assigns and both DB-backed histories, supplying a separate resynchronization path for incoming joins.

metrics_verification.script: metrics.py read but not run, because it overwrites metrics.json. Independently recomputed from complete retained JSONL sessions.
metrics_verification.total: input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite equals recorded totalTokens in every assistant response. CacheWrite is zero throughout. Reasoning is already included in output/recorded total, do not add it again.
metrics_verification.cost: Sums every assistant usage.cost.total including cache. Recorded rates: $2/M input, $10/M output, $0.10/M cacheRead. This is Pi/provider-reported estimated cost, not independently verified invoices.
metrics_verification.errors: ToolErrors sums toolResult.isError only, not provider-error assistant messages or every unsuccessful subcommand; separate provider-error counts retained above. Zero-usage provider errors have unknown unreported backend consumption.
metrics_verification.tool_result_bytes: JSON-serialized tool-result content bytes, not token count.
metrics_verification.finished: Last assistant stopReason is stop in all nine.

protocol_limitations: One repetition per cell, three purposively chosen tasks; no statistical or universal ranking. Checkpoints were defined from production source before reading measured answers; compound checkpoints use explicit behavioral coverage, not exact wording.

All nine sessions overlap in time, causing shared provider/host contention; EX-GRAPHIFY has four provider errors, PY-ATLAS and PY-PLAIN one each. Elapsed time is first user message to final assistant message, includes retries and answer/metadata/memory saving; not pure CLI latency or wall-clock batch duration.

Same research model gpt-6.1-sol and medium reasoning verified for all assistant messages/settings; initial model-change metadata mentions gpt-5.6-terra before switching, with no research messages on that model. Each retained session has one user prompt and no inherited conversation shown; provider prompt cache can still be shared across fresh contexts.
Pilot native batch used --no-session, so its metrics were discarded. Only measured/ answers and complete retained sessions are scored; results/ was not used.

Pilot Graphify save-result/reflections were not reset before measured runs (reported protocol defect). Actual measured calls contain no reflect/LESSONS/pilot memory reads, and query responses show source graph retrieval, not prior answers. EX saves new memory only after drafting. This limits observed contamination concern but does not repair the unreset experimental condition.

All source/index/cache state was warm from setup/pilot. Prompt cache usage varied too: TS-GRAPHIFY first response used 6016 cached input and 254 uncached versus 6269 uncached in several other arms. Token totals and estimated cost therefore measure this warm run, not cold-start requirements.

Graphify setup is detect(code)->AST extract->directed build->cluster->JSON, with sql extra installed, not full semantic-document/label/visualization skill pipeline. Python corpus is 727 code files, deliberately bypassing >500-file narrowing. Documents/images excluded; Atlas and Graphify do not have identical language/file universes.

Graphify query traversal intentionally explores both edge directions even though corpus is directed; path/explain preserve directed semantics. No path and truncated retrieval are not absence proofs, which answers generally acknowledge. All Graphify arms visibly use query/explain, TS/EX path; none performs substantive callflow beyond help.

Graphify query skill is only partially followed: vocab expansion and budgeted queries yes, start-of-work reflection absent in all three and save-result absent PY/TS. Thus this is not a strict full-skill efficacy evaluation.

Setup timers measure Atlas migration+index and Graphify detection/extraction/clustering/export, not installation; archive extraction precedes Atlas timer, diagnostics follow Graphify timer. No install timings were instrumented. Plain has no index build, but shares warm sources.

All source verification allowed; graph arms still depend heavily on source reads. Harness calls batch CLI operations; submitted shell command counts include cd/export/printf/env/tests/Python helpers and short-circuited commands. They are not exact executed syscall or file-read counts. Python helpers can read many files per operation.

Precision is not completeness: 12-point coverage scores do not estimate fraction of true claims. Material contradictions and diagram edges are listed separately; representative citation checks are not an exhaustive citation-accuracy rate.

conclusions.tokens_cost: Observed aggregate Plain < Atlas < Graphify for uncached I/O, total tokens and reported cost. EX uncached I/O is Atlas < Plain, but cost favors Plain; do not conflate token categories.
conclusions.cli_operations: Atlas executes 58 graph CLI invocations versus Graphify 24 including help/save and Plain zero graph CLI. Submitted shell totals are 144/56/49 respectively, plus one nested Graphify subprocess. Native source/prompt/skill reads are 18/48/55; no fair single effective-operation winner can be inferred from harness calls alone.
conclusions.time: Aggregate summed cell time Plain < Atlas < Graphify; PY Graphify fastest, TS Atlas fastest, EX Plain fastest. Provider retries especially penalize EX Graphify.
conclusions.coverage: Graphify 36/36; Atlas and Plain 35/36. PY/TS all 12/12; EX Graphify 12/12 and others 11/12 due omitted session-notification reload. Ceiling checklist result is not claim precision.
conclusions.precision: Prose behavior largely tied and correct; Graphify has cleanest material diagram audit, but small TS layout attribution issue and weaker line citations. Atlas has strongest representative citation accuracy but one misleading EX production edge; Plain has one misleading EX production edge and TS citation offsets. No defensible numerical precision ratio or universal precision winner.
conclusions.overall: No universal winner. For these warm tasks Plain is cheapest and aggregate fastest; Atlas minimizes harness calls, not CLI operations; Graphify adds one explicit synchronization checkpoint and cleaner EX diagram at higher aggregate cost. Repetition/cold-state reset needed for broader claims.
